notes: HE 0437-5439 is grouped among the 16 HVSs found by earlier surveys and is called an HVS in the paper (T:p1-b7; T:p3-b12), so it is classified as follow_up. SDSS J1403+1450, SDSS J1546+2437, SDSS J0940+5309, and SDSS J1014+5631 are expressly described as prior “four other HVS candidates listed in Brown et al. (2009a)” and are given conditional treatment (T:p5-b1), so they are also follow_up. Only named stars are listed; the remaining members of the 16-HVS sample appear as unlabeled points in the figures (I:p4-b4; I:p4-b5) and are not individually identifiable from the supplied material. The explicitly bound “hypervelocity” stars, including SDSS J1404+3522, are not treated as Galactic unbound candidates (T:p5-b1).

HE 0437-5439: HE 0437-5439 is mentioned only qualitatively in T:p3-b12: it is the one HVS "neither on the CWS plane nor on the Narm plane," suggested to have been ejected from the LMC. The paper reports no numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star.

SDSS J1403+1450: SDSS J1403+1450 is identified in the paper only as one of four HVS candidates from Brown et al. (2009a). The sole star-specific statement is in T:p5-b1: "two of them (SDSS J1403+1450 and SDSS J1546+2437) are within ~16° to the CWS plane". This is an angular offset from a fitted plane, not any of the requested quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability). No individual coordinates, distances, velocities, or probabilities are reported for this star; its position is only displayed graphically in Fig. 4 (I:p4-b5), with no numeric values. Therefore no eligible quantities are extracted.

SDSS J1546+2437: SDSS J1546+2437 is mentioned only qualitatively in T:p5-b1 as one of four HVS candidates, stated to be within ~16° of the CWS plane; it is also plotted as a carmine star in Fig. 4 (I:p4-b5). The paper reports no individual numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star. The ~16° value is a sky-plane angular separation, not one of the requested quantities, so no quantities are retained.

SDSS J0940+5309: The target star SDSS J0940+5309 is mentioned only once in the paper (T:p5-b1), as one of the four HVS candidates listed by Brown et al. (2009a); the authors state that it lies "within 3° to the Narm plane" (along with SDSS J1014+5631). No individual astrometric, kinematic, distance, velocity, probability, or plane-normal values are reported for this star. Figure 4 (I:p4-b5) merely plots the candidates as carmine stars without labeling individual coordinates. Therefore no eligible quantity values can be extracted for this target.

SDSS J1014+5631: SDSS J1014+5631 is mentioned in T:p5-b1 only as one of the four HVS candidates from Brown et al. (2009a), stated to be "within ~3° to the Narm plane" and plotted in Figure 4 (I:p4-b5). The paper reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this individual star, so no target quantities can be extracted.
